name: Anvil
description: A steel anvil with a flat face, a horn for bending and a hardy hole for fitting tools.
notes: London-pattern anvil built by the shared `anvil(s)` helper in the batch file: splayed foot, waist, body with a steel-bright face plate on iron-dull, a step before the horn, hardy and pritchel holes painted flush in coal-black. 520 mm horn to heel and 200 mm high. Too heavy to carry far, so it works as a workstation where it is set down.

name: Bronze anvil
description: A cast bronze anvil, softer than steel but serviceable for shaping hot metal.
notes: Shares the steel anvil's model and size; only the finishes differ (bronze body, bronze-polished face). Same 26 kg mass as the reference.

name: Small anvil
description: A small but properly shaped anvil, light enough to move between jobs.
notes: London-pattern anvil built by the shared `anvil(s)` helper in the batch file: splayed foot, waist, body with a steel-bright face plate on iron-dull, a step before the horn, hardy and pritchel holes painted flush in coal-black. Scaled to 300 mm long and 120 mm high; box/volume x1.6 is the horn and waist around the solid body.

name: Heavy anvil
description: A massive smithy anvil with a broad face and long horn, built for heavy forging.
notes: London-pattern anvil built by the shared `anvil(s)` helper in the batch file: splayed foot, waist, body with a steel-bright face plate on iron-dull, a step before the horn, hardy and pritchel holes painted flush in coal-black. Scaled to 970 mm long and 380 mm high for 225 kg. It stays where it stands, so it carries a workstation block. The flecks on the face in the tile are the voxel outline of the steel-bright face plate, not modelled detail.

name: Scavenged anvil
description: A slab cut from heavy machinery, its top ground flat to serve as an anvil.
notes: 400 by 200 mm and 150 mm high: a steel-parkerized block on a bolt flange, a steel-bright ground top with one rounded end for bending, torch-cut end in steel-heat-tint, bolt bosses, and patches of old paint-olive paint and rust-red. Box/volume x0.40: the reference volume is CDDA's carry volume, smaller than a block this mass (50 kg of steel is about 6.4 L, which the box matches).

name: Stump anvil
description: A thick log with steel plates and a bar bolted to its top, good for light hammer work.
notes: 260 mm across and 330 mm high with the plates: a bark-sided stump, sawn wood-pine top with a growth ring, two steel-grey plates and a steel-bright bar bolted on with iron-dull bolt heads.

name: Bolt cutters
description: Long-handled cutters with short hardened jaws. They bite through padlock shackles and heavy wire.
notes: 460 mm long lying along x, jaws closed at +x: plastic-red grips on steel-grey arms, a steel-blued head with steel-bright pivot bolts and steel-hardened jaws. Gripped on one grip. CHECK VOLUME (box/volume x0.27): the reference's 2.75 L is a carry volume; the closed tool is a thin 460 by 80 by 22 mm. The quality name `metal_cutting` is new; CDDA lists none for this item.

name: Sand casting mould
description: A two-part wooden flask packed with sand around a cavity, with a pouring cup and a riser on top.
notes: Flask 400 by 260 mm and 200 mm high in wood-oak, a lower drag and upper cope split by a dark parting line, brick-buff sand (no sand finish exists) with coal-black pouring cup and riser, steel-grey alignment pins in end lugs. The small, large and long sandcasting moulds share this model as variants; their size and mass differ (6, 76.6 and 37 kg).

name: Charcoal forge
description: A portable steel forge pan with a firepot and a hand-cranked blower to drive the coals hot.
notes: 560 by 280 mm and 200 mm high: a paint-charcoal pan on four legs, a firepot of coal-black charcoal with a glow-flame ember, a steel-grey air pipe to a paint-oxblood blower with a wooden crank. Box/volume x3.9 is the open pan and blower around a thin sheet body.

name: Drum charcoal kiln
description: A steel drum with a clamped lid, a short chimney and air holes at the foot, for turning wood into charcoal.
notes: 580 mm across and 1050 mm high with the chimney: an open-head drum from `h.drum` in iron-dull with a clamped lid, a steel-galvanised chimney and four coal-black air holes round the foot. Box/volume x2.0 is the round drum and chimney in their box. Deployed in place, so it carries a workstation block.

name: Cold chisel
description: A short, stout steel chisel for cutting and shaping metal under a hammer.
notes: 200 mm long from 19 mm bar: a steel-heat-tint mushroomed head, a steel-grey shank and a ground steel-bright edge at +x. Box/volume x0.32: the reference's 250 mL is a carry volume; the bar itself is about 60 mL. The bronze and stone chisels share this model with their own finishes.

name: Bronze chisel
description: A cast bronze chisel, softer than steel but able to cut and shape metal.
notes: Variant of the cold chisel on the shared model with bronze finishes; 0.735 kg.

name: Stone chisel
description: A chisel ground from hard stone, crude but usable for shaping.
notes: Variant of the cold chisel on the shared model with stone-grey finishes; 0.6 kg. A knapped stone would be lumpier than the turned steel bar, but the shape reads at this size.

name: Crucible
description: A thick-walled ceramic pot with a pouring lip, for melting metal in a forge.
notes: 165 mm high and 135 mm across, ceramic-grey with a pouring lip and a coal-black dross layer on its floor. Box/volume x1.7 is the round pot in its box.

name: Clay crucible
description: A hand-made fired clay pot with a pouring lip, for melting metal.
notes: Shares the crucible's model with clay-terracotta finishes; 1.642 kg.

name: Crude bronze nail
description: A rough cast bronze nail with a lumpy head.
notes: 40 mm long: a round bronze head and a tapering square shank. One nail per item; Deadvox can stack them. Box/volume x3.2 is the head standing proud of a 5 mm shank.

name: Draw plate
description: A steel plate pierced with rows of shrinking holes. Pulling wire through them draws it thinner.
notes: 160 by 40 by 8 mm, steel-grey with two rows of coal-black holes stepping down from 9 mm to 3 mm. CHECK VOLUME (box/volume x0.20): the reference's 250 mL is a carry volume; the plate itself is 51 mL.
